Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you write a short update for Mina, not Idris, about what happened at the neighborhood weather station this morning? Make it a note from volunteer Joel rather than a public bulletin. He arrived at 7:10 and found leaves caught in the rain gauge’s outer funnel. He cleared them, then poured the water already collected into the measuring cylinder; it measured 6 mm from overnight rain. Please mention that Joel wrote the measurement in the station log before leaving at 7:35. The station is on Alder Street, and the note should say that he noticed the blockage when he checked the gauge during his usual morning visit. Keep it to about two paragraphs, with a calm, straightforward tone. Include the times and measurement accurately, and make clear the 6 mm was the amount collected overnight, not a forecast. Don’t turn it into a general weather report or make it sound like anyone else was there. Just a concise account of this one visit, addressed to Mina, not Idris.", "output": "Write a concise, two-paragraph note from volunteer Joel to Mina, not Idris, about his morning visit to the neighborhood weather station on Alder Street. Use a calm, straightforward tone and make it a personal update, not a public bulletin or general weather report.\n\nInclude these details: Joel arrived at 7:10 for his usual morning visit and found leaves caught in the rain gauge’s outer funnel. He cleared the leaves, poured the water already collected into the measuring cylinder, and measured 6 mm from overnight rain. He recorded the measurement in the station log before leaving at 7:35. Present the 6 mm as the amount collected overnight, not as a forecast, and do not imply that anyone else was there."}]
